request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user the due-totals of the people they watch, added up (0.00 when
watching no one).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now shows a "Watched due total" (`watched-due-total`): the due-totals of the people the signed-in user watches, added up, or `0.00` when they watch no one. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `PORT=3010 bin/e2e`.

**The change** is front-end only, in `src/main/frontend/features/header/header.slot.tsx`. The server already returns which people a user watches, so nothing new was needed in the stored data or server. The header reads that list and adds up the same per-person due-total shown on each person's row. If someone in the list is no longer on the sheet, they don't count.

**Port problem on this machine:** your shell sets `PORT=3002`, but another copy of this app, started on Oct 23 (pid 990954), is already using that port. So a plain `bin/e2e` here can't start its own app, and the tests talk to the old one and fail on the first form they submit. I didn't stop that process because it isn't mine. Running with a free port fixes it: `PORT=3010 bin/e2e`. Ports 3003 and 3004 also have copies of the app running.
